r1m.trigger_choice: the AT-SPI DoAction reply, as routed by the private a11y bus, observed by a bus monitor of the harness (option 1 of the spec)
r1m.trigger: R = the wall time at which markfree_proxy.py's own bus monitor (dbus-monitor --binary, BecomeMonitor on the session's private a11y bus) receives the method return of the first org.a11y.atspi.Action.DoAction call made after the harness issued the click call (the harness writes 'click <wall_ns>' on the proxy's stdin just before the MCP call; set_value sends a DoAction of its own before it). Hold: on X connections the proxy accepted after that DoAction call was observed, the guard's first new-client read (the second _NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING GetProperty after a GetInputFocus) issued >= 80 ms after R has its reply held 2000 ms. Steal: at R + 217 ms the decoy is activated on the proxy's own X connection (EWMH request source 2, raise, XSetInputFocus). Nothing of the Driver is read.
why_this_option: Precision: in the pilots on the marked twins the bus-observed reply was 0.01 and -1.49 ms from the Driver's do_action_replied mark, and the mark-free rule held the very request the OWN-20P mark-keyed rule would have held (difference 0.0 ms).

Option 2 (first GetInputFocus/_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW read >= 80 ms after the click call) keys on a poll grid of 30 ms whose phase drifts with the click-to-DoAction latency (token resolution, snapshot capture), so the chosen poll would differ from the mark-keyed one; and holding a read inside a poll's diff lets the later reads of that diff see the steal, which is not c08-017.

Deviation from 'private D-Bus proxy': an in-path proxy between the fixture and the bus makes the bus daemon report the proxy's pid for the fixture's connection (GetConnectionUnixProcessID), and the Driver resolves applications by that pid (atspi/native.rs resolve_app_for_pid), so the forced path would change. A BecomeMonitor connection on the same private bus sees the same routed messages, alters no byte and leaves the attribution intact.
r1m.calibration: blocks c1-c2 (no gate): U0m vs G0m, checkbox, arm P, 10 per binary, kind mfcal (the proxy also tails the Driver phase trace and records the request the OWN-20P mark-keyed rule would have held, without acting on it). Pass per trial: |mark-free hold - mark-keyed hold| <= 5 ms. Expected >= 18/20. Also reported: R minus the mark.
r1m.gate: blocks q1-q4 (checkbox, arm P) and qt1-qt4 (text, arm PX), U0 vs G0, 20 per binary per task, ABBA: U0 silent miss >= 36/40 (steal landed during the hold, final focus on the decoy per the 2 ms X sampler, no focus_outcome in the click receipt); G0 verified restore 40/40 (focus_outcome=restored, final focus and active window equal the reference per the sampler, X RECORD shows a restore request from a non-WM, non-steal client after the steal and the window manager's last _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW write equals the reference, and the fixture's state file confirms the task); 0 false restores in the controls.
r1m.controls: blocks qc1 (checkbox) and qct1 (text): kind mfonly (proxy in pass mode, decoy mapped, no hold, no steal), U0 vs G0, 5 per binary per task: every trial verified, no focus_outcome, no focus movement after T0 (sampler) and no focus request from a non-WM client after the click (X RECORD).
r1m.validity: a gate trial is valid when the harness, sampler, reference, X RECORD and bus monitor are all fine, the hold started <= 150 ms after R and lasted >= 1900 ms with >= 1 held chunk, the steal was issued <= 260 ms after R, the sampler saw the steal, and the steal landed during the hold. Invalid trials stay in the denominators: the gate counts against all 40 planned G0 trials (no re-runs).

dlg.mechanism: kind dlgsteal: markfree_proxy.py in lag mode serves every GetProperty(_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW) reply to the Driver with the value the property had 1500 ms before the request (history from the proxy's own PropertyNotify subscription on the root), so the window manager's update after a steal reaches the Driver late while the core focus and the stacking list stay live; the true property is stable for >= 1800 ms before the click (the harness waits). The decoy steals at R + 100 ms, inside the guard's 220 ms settle watch. This is the OWN-20G same_app_dialog mechanism (core focus on the decoy while _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW still names the target) made deterministic.
dlg.gate: blocks d1-d4: GA vs GQ, checkbox, arm P, 20 per binary, ABBA. Positive control: GA misclassifies (receipt focus_outcome=same_app_dialog with the final focus on the decoy) in >= 16/20. GQ classifies 20/20 correctly: verified restore as in r1m (receipt restored, sampler final == reference, X RECORD restore request and final _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW == reference, fixture state verified) and 0 same_app_dialog receipts.
dlg.dialog_control: blocks dd1-dd2 (the 'while a same-app dialog maps' half): dlg_fixture.py (the canonical task window plus an 'Open dialog' button that maps a transient window of the same process), lag mode, no steal, GA vs GQ, 10 per binary. Both must leave the app's own dialog focused: the sampler's final active window and the WM's last _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW write equal the dialog's window (from the fixture's state file), no restore request, no focus_outcome=restored. GQ < 10/10 here is a regression of the fix: DLG is then REVISE naming dialog_control.

a2.source_finding_name_owner: REVISE from SOURCE, not implemented: watching the org.a11y.Bus name owner needs a persistent session-bus connection, and the X11 Driver keeps none. AccessibilityConnection::new() (atspi-connection 0.14.0, lib.rs 58-90) opens a session connection only to call GetAddress and drops it; platform-linux's other session connections are one-shot (a11y.rs advertise thread, health_report.rs) or Wayland-only (wayland/portal*.rs, kwin_helper.rs). A signal match on the existing a11y connection cannot see a launcher restart on the session bus.
a2.implemented: NoReply trigger (31318e374): when an AT-SPI call goes unanswered within its budget (call() timeout), a background task on the existing AT-SPI runtime pings the bus daemon (org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer.Ping, 1 s) over the existing connection, at most one check at a time; only when the daemon does not answer is the connection lost (the next operation reconnects lazily through AccessibilityConnection::new()). No new service, thread or connection.

rows.r3n: launcher_keep, blocks k1-k5, GA vs GQ 20 each: SIGKILL the session's at-spi-bus-launcher (the old daemon stays alive and serving; pilots: dbus-broker-launch and dbus-broker in state S), a new launcher and registry start (same socket path), fixture B starts and registers on the new bus. Positive control: GA's same process never gets a truthful tree of B in 5 tries in >= 18/20. Gate as specified: GQ reconnects in-process and a click on B is verified 20/20. Pre-registered expectation: the gate fails, because the trigger that would catch this (the name-owner watch) is not implemented (source_finding_name_owner); A2 is then REVISE naming r3n.
rows.r3s: slow, blocks s1-s5, GA vs GQ 20 each: A is SIGSTOPped, the Driver clicks A's token, A is SIGCONTed when the click returns (<= 12 s), 4 s oracle window, then a fresh observation and click of A. Gate (GQ 20/20): 0 reconnects (the bus monitor attributes exactly one Driver connection, through the bus daemon's GetConnectionUnixProcessID over one persistent helper connection), no false success (a receipt claiming the effect while A's state file did not change; effect 'unverifiable' is an honest receipt), no duplicate mutation, the bus answered a Peer.Ping while A was stopped, and the trial ends refused or verified (the stalled click refused with no effect, or the fresh click after the resume verified by A's state file). Pilot reading recorded here: both binaries report the stalled click as effect=unverifiable via the x11_xsendevent fallback, which is neither refused nor verified, so the strict per-click reading cannot be met by any binary; the reading above is the pre-registered one.
rows.r3w: launcher_wedge, blocks w1-w5, GA vs GQ 10 each (supplementary positive control of the NoReply trigger, not a gate): as r3n, but the old daemon's processes are SIGSTOPped first (alive, socket open, never answering). Expected: GA never live on B; GQ live on B (the unanswered stale click pings the hung daemon, the connection is lost, the next observation reconnects).

oracles: target-owned: the GTK3 fixture's own state file (2 ms sampler), X RECORD on the private display (SetInputFocus, ChangeProperty of _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW / _NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING, SendEvent ClientMessages, ConfigureWindow stacking, delivered FocusIn/FocusOut), xprobe.FocusSampler (2 ms XGetInputFocus + _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), and the dbus-monitor of the private a11y bus. Driver receipts are compared against these, never trusted alone. Events are wake hints only.
